message: `/` in the body of `divides`, which claims `restrict(no-trap)`
help: `no-trap` is LOCAL, like `no-cast` and `no-wrap`: on `Int` operands `/` and `%` trap on a zero divisor (exit 72) and on the `INT_MIN / -1` corner (exit 83), and `<<` and `>>` trap on an out-of-range shift amount (exit 84) - so the trapping use is an act this body performs by writing the raw operator, not a fact the effect row or call graph carries. `stdlib/Err.ax` has the checked alternative for each: `divChecked`, `remChecked`, `shlChecked`, `shrChecked`, every one `(-> Int Int (Result Int Error))`. Calling one pulls `Alloc` into this body's effect row (constructing the `Result` allocates), so `no-trap` cannot be satisfied together with `no-alloc` or `pure` by a body that needs these operations - write the checked call and match its `Err`, accept the row, or delete the tag. ONE SPELLING IS NOT REFUSED: `/` on `Float` operands, which lowers to `fdiv` with no integer trap to require, and whose checked fix is `(-> Int Int (Result Int Error))` and does not typecheck against a `Float`
